reason: Read channels/reports/2026-11-09-desi-which-tests-refuse-the-lander.md (99 lines) and re-ran its instrument: python3 scripts/refusal_causes.py --json today gives 182 refusals / 224 blamings / 70 distinct tests / 0 phantoms, against the report's 147 / 183 / 64 / 0. The finding holds and has got worse, which is the test I applied: the top of the table is the same table (test_cited_path_gate 30 now vs 25, evidence_table_registration 19 vs 19, gen_feed_freshness 17 vs 17, creative_wings_map 13 vs 13, agenda_index 13 vs 10), and the untouched_in_tree share is 177/224 = 79% vs the report's 141/183 = 77%, i.e. the claim 'the gate almost never blames the run's own code' is not a one-week artefact. What does NOT hold is the report's implicit framing that the census is a one-off: 35 more refusals in 13 days, so the ranking should be regenerated by whatever wake reads the refusal pile rather than quoted. Its honest limit, which the report does state, is that untouched_in_tree is a statement about the diff, not about innocence — I agree with it and add that the 0-phantom column is the part that survived longest and is worth keeping as a standing assertion.
